data.title: Apple shares rise after iPhone Duo pre-orders sell out within minutes
data.description:
Apple AAPL shares edged higher after the company's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, sold out shortly after preorders opened on Friday.

At 11:05 AM EST, the stock was trading around $346.46, up approximately 1.3% from Thursday's close, as investors assessed the initial response to Apple's long-awaited entry into the foldable phone segment.

Users on social media reported that estimated delivery dates for the new device had shifted from October 23 to late January, suggesting that initial demand was running ahead of available supply.

Sentiments were also helped by other company-specific developments.

iPhone Duo marks Apple's entry into foldables

Apple has entered the foldable smartphone market after lagging behind Samsung and Chinese manufacturers in the category.

The passport-sized iPhone Duo features a 5.4-inch front display and a 7.6-inch foldable internal screen. Apple expects foldable smartphones to account for roughly 10% of the market by 2029.

The initial response to the device could help the company establish a foothold in the segment, although preorder demand alone does not determine the product's eventual sales performance.

The launch also comes as Apple seeks to diversify its growth drivers beyond its established iPhone lineup.

The reported weakness in demand for the iPhone 18 Pro models had raised concerns about the outlook for its premium smartphones, making the reception of the foldable device an important development for investors.

Apple Intelligence clears regulatory hurdle in China

In another development, Apple Chairman Tim Cook announced during a visit to Shanghai that Apple Intelligence had received regulatory clearance from Chinese authorities.

The software is expected to begin rolling out to users in China as a test version later in October. Planned features include writing assistance, photo cleanup, and live translation.

To comply with local requirements, Apple has partnered with Chinese e-commerce company Alibaba to use its Qwen AI models for users in mainland China.

Apple and Meta collaborate

Apple is also collaborating with Meta to optimize the latter's new Muse Spark Open AI model for Apple's high-end Mac computers.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg publicly thanked Apple's engineering team for helping optimize the model to run on M5 Ultra Mac computers.

The collaboration focuses on enabling Meta's large open-weight AI model to run locally on Apple's high-end Mac Studio desktop systems.

The partnership signals a potential shift in the relationship between the companies, which have previously clashed over issues including data privacy and App Store fees.

Under Apple CEO John Ternus and Meta CEO Zuckerberg, the work brings the two technology companies together on AI infrastructure and model performance.

Analysts largely bullish but demand concerns weigh

Analysts remain bullish over Apple's stock prospects, but there are some concerns as well.

UBS maintained its Neutral rating on Apple with a $296 price target, pointing to iPhone availability data showing shorter waiting times than a year earlier.

The firm viewed the decline in wait times, alongside a stable supply backdrop, as a concern for the iPhone maker.

KeyBanc also maintained an Underweight rating on the stock, reflecting a more cautious outlook.

JP Morgan, however, said the reported reductions in iPhone 18 Pro production orders were consistent with the adjustments Apple typically makes each year.

The post Apple shares rise after iPhone Duo pre-orders sell out within minutes appeared first on Invezz

data.title: CoreWeave stock drops nearly 20% this week. Why analysts say its a buy
data.description:
CoreWeave stock CRWV fell again on Friday after recovering in the previous session, putting the AI cloud computing company on track for a steep weekly loss as investors continued to worry about its debt-financed expansion amid rising borrowing costs.

The stock dropped about 7.2% on Friday, even as the S&P 500 edged higher.

Nasdaq Composite opened lower by about 0.4%.

CoreWeave shares have lost nearly 20% this week as concerns over inflation, interest rates and the financing requirements of artificial intelligence infrastructure weighed on sentiment.

In addition, Gartner released research indicating that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will most likely cease independent operations.

Rising borrowing costs put debt under scrutiny

For some analysts, CoreWeave has become a symbol of the debt-fuelled AI infrastructure boom, in which companies are committing billions of dollars to data centres and computing capacity before the long-term returns on that investment are fully established.

The sell-off intensified after hotter-than-expected US inflation data on Wednesday heightened concerns that interest rates could remain elevated, increasing the cost of financing capital-intensive AI infrastructure.

Nicholas Mugalli, chief investment officer at World Trade Securities, said CoreWeave short sellers made around $806 million in paper profit on Wednesday when the stock fell 15.5%.

CoreWeave's $2.8 billion of 9.75% bonds issued in April traded at 79.5 cents on the dollar on Thursday, yielding more than 15%, according to data provided by BondCliQ.

The loss-making cloud computing company has about $50 billion in debt.

"A hot inflation print triggered a ​sharp selloff in CoreWeave because its business model is a highly indebted play on future data center demand," BCA Research analysts said.

"Although the rest ​of the tech complex is also sensitive to the ​pace and magnitude of AI adoption and use, it is, on average, ‌considerably ⁠less sensitive to interest rates"

CoreWeave rents out Nvidia graphics processing units and supplies computing power to AI laboratories such as OpenAI and major technology companies including Meta Platforms.

It operates data centres across the US and internationally.

The business depends on continued demand for computing capacity, while its expansion requires substantial upfront investment.

That combination has left investors weighing the strength of its contracted revenue against the risks associated with its debt and future capital expenditure.

Why neoclouds face a threat, but CoreWeave is likely to survive

Gartner said in 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030, but enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period.

A cumulative $8.5 trillion in revenue would be required to recover the massive AI spend, according to Gartner; however, total enterprise and consumer AI revenue that can be attributed to AI data centers during this period is forecast to reach no more than $3.6 trillion, it said.

"Failure to achieve sustainable ROIC on rapidly depreciating assets would almost certainly necessitate write-downs," it said.

Neoclouds will be among the most exposed to the imbalance between revenue and capital spending, and cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model will force over 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations, it said.

Melvin, Milk Road analyst, agreed but said CoreWeave and Nebius will be the top survivors.

"The majority of neocloud companies will NOT survive. I strongly believe we're going to see a MASSIVE amount of consolidation across this industry over the next several years, and only a handful of companies will come out on top," Melvin said.

"Personally, I think $CRWV and $NBIS will be the top 2," he said.

Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang, whose company is CoreWeave's second-largest investor with an approximately 10% stake, sought to reassure investors about its financial position.

"CoreWeave’s financial strength is improving every day," Huang told reporters at an event in Stockholm, adding that he did not see a need for Nvidia to backstop the company.

"I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing."

Analysts see buying opportunity

Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated its Overweight rating on CoreWeave, with a $176 price target implying upside of more than 150% from its reference price.

The firm said CoreWeave had public support from Nvidia and had sold nearly all the capacity scheduled to come online in 2027.

Nvidia has an agreement to backstop any unsold capacity.

According to Cantor Fitzgerald, the principal concern is whether CoreWeave can finance the capital expenditure required to meet demand, rather than whether demand for AI computing exists.

The firm described the current period as an attractive opportunity to add to or initiate a position in the shares.

Deutsche Bank also maintained its Buy rating on CoreWeave, with a $150 price target, implying upside of more than 100% from its reference price.

Analyst Brad Zelnick acknowledged that the company's prospects are closely tied to the performance of the AI sector and demand for computing infrastructure.

He argued, however, that its underlying contracts provide meaningful support.

“The vast majority of CoreWeave’s backlog is associated with long-term take-or-pay contracts where contracted revenue fully covers all capital and operating costs associated with the contract and generates a return for the company,” Zelnick wrote.

He estimated that 60% to 65% of CoreWeave's backlog was tied to investment-grade customers at the end of the second quarter.

The company has used these contracts to secure project-specific debt at costs at or below its parent company's borrowing rate.

“A strong customer base, established record of execution, backlog conversion and leading infrastructure performance is all supportive of their issuer profile relative to neocloud peers, in our view,” Zelnick said.

Deutsche Bank also highlighted CoreWeave's financing arrangements and liquidity position.

“Available liquidity stood at $15.5 billion, and since that time the company: closed a $2.6 billion DDTL 5.5 (backed by shorter 3-yr contracts) at SOFR + 5.50%; closed a $4.2 billion 2.875% Convertible Senior Note and announced a 35 million share ATM equity program,” the bank said.

Capital needs remain a key risk

Despite the positive assessment of its customer contracts, CoreWeave faces substantial funding requirements as it expands its infrastructure.

Deutsche Bank forecasts operating cash flow of about $10 billion over the next 12 months, compared with required capital expenditure of roughly $45 billion.

That gap means the company will need to secure additional funding, although Zelnick argued it could raise capital at a steady pace, supported by its contracted customer backlog.

The central question for investors is whether CoreWeave can convert its substantial order book into cash flow quickly enough to support its expansion without putting further pressure on its balance sheet.

For now, bullish analysts see long-term contracts, investment-grade customers and Nvidia's support as reasons to look beyond the recent sell-off.

More cautious investors remain focused on the cost of financing the infrastructure boom and the risks of relying on future demand to justify heavy borrowing.

data.title: Netflix stock falls 3% as content shake-up fails to ease investor worries
data.description:
Netflix shares NFLX fell 3.5% in premarket trading on Friday after the streaming company announced a leadership change aimed at strengthening its film and television programming amid slowing viewer engagement and increased competition.

The company said former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice would become its chief content officer on October 26, replacing Bela Bajaria, who is leaving after nearly a decade at Netflix.

The announcement came a day after the company revealed plans to cut approximately 6% of its workforce, or around 1,000 jobs.

Netflix shares had already declined 23% this year through Thursday's close, as concerns about its share of television viewing and ability to produce popular content weighed on investor sentiment.

Netflix replaces Bela Bajaria with Peter Rice

Rice will oversee Netflix's film and television slate, as well as live events, taking responsibility for a broad range of programming as the company seeks to improve viewer engagement.

He previously managed Disney's television operations, including ABC, FX, Hulu and its television studios.

Before joining Disney, Rice held senior positions at 21st Century Fox and Fox Searchlight Pictures.

During his tenure at Disney, the company released critically acclaimed programmes such as Modern Family and Abbott Elementary and approved projects including The Bear.

Netflix co-chief executive Ted Sarandos praised Rice's industry experience and relationships with Hollywood talent, describing him as one of the entertainment industry's most effective large-scale operators.

Sarandos also thanked Bajaria for helping expand Netflix's programming into unscripted shows, live events and sports.

Bajaria had overseen the company's global film and television slate since 2023.

The leadership change comes as Netflix explores new programming formats, including video podcasts and live sports, to compete for audiences against platforms such as YouTube and TikTok.

Viewer engagement and competition weigh on shares

Netflix has faced concerns that its share of television viewing hours is declining, raising questions about whether slowing engagement could eventually affect subscriber growth.

The company has struggled to produce cultural hits on the scale of earlier successes such as Stranger Things and Wednesday.

Finding another globally popular programme could help restore momentum, although the performance of future releases remains uncertain.

Sarandos acknowledged the challenge at a conference last month, saying: “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster.”

Netflix also drew scrutiny in July when it announced that it would publish its engagement report once a year instead of twice a year, starting in 2027.

Competition for viewers has intensified as established streaming services and digital platforms vie for audiences' time.

The company had also sought to expand its programming library through a potential acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, but Paramount, now called Skydance, ultimately won the bidding contest.

Job cuts and upcoming earnings in focus

The appointment of Rice follows Netflix's announcement that it would eliminate around 1,000 positions, marking its largest round of layoffs in at least four years.

The combination of job cuts and a leadership transition highlights the pressure on the company to improve operating efficiency while strengthening its content offering.

Rice's priorities will include Netflix's film and television productions and live events.

Industry insiders are also watching for his decisions on key leadership roles and the performance of major upcoming projects, including La Bola Negra and Narnia, which are associated with current film chair Dan Lin.

Netflix is scheduled to report earnings on Tuesday, giving investors an opportunity to assess its latest financial performance and management's outlook.

The company's ability to improve viewer engagement and deliver successful programming will remain central to its efforts to rebuild investor confidence and reverse its share-price decline.

Wedbush reiterated its buy position on the stock while cutting the target price from $105 to $90.

BMO Capital also maintained its buy position and slashed the target price from $135 to $125.

data.title: Top FTSE 100 shares to watch: Barclays, Unilever, Persimmon, Aberdeen Group
data.description:
The FTSE 100 has rallied strongly over the past few weeks, climbing from a low of 10,370 earlier this month to around 10,820. That momentum will be in focus next week as investors turn their attention to key UK economic data and earnings reports from major companies.

UK to publish important macro data

The FTSE 100 will react to some important numbers from the UK. The Office of National Statistics (ONS) will publish the latest jobs numbers on Tuesday. After that, the agency will release the September consumer inflation data on Wednesday. 

Economists expect the data to show that the headline and core CPI jumped in September as energy prices soared. Finally, the UK will release the official retail sales report, which are expected to show that volume rose in September. 

These numbers will help the Bank of England (BoE) when delivering its interest rate decision later this month. Economists expect the bank to hike interest rates later this month.

Barclays stock in focus as it releases earnings

BARC stock has been under pressure in the past few months as concerns about the investment banking division rose. After starting the year well, there are signs that the trend is getting worse, with the volume of deals falling by over 40% sequentially in the third quarter.

The severity of this issue was seen this week when US banks like Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Bank of America. Morgan Stanley’s investment banking revenue rose by just 2% to $2.16 billion, $110 million lower than expected. 

Analysts expect that Barclays UK will have a profit before tax of 931 million pounds, with its UK corporate bank making 291 million pounds. Its private bank and wealth management division is expected to make 99 million pounds.

Unilever

Unilever stock has staged a strong comeback in the past few months. It has jumped from a low of 4,000p earlier this year to the current 4,885p. This rally will be in the spotlight as investors react to its upcoming earnings report.

These results will provide hints on how the company is doing. The last earnings report showed that its sales growth rose 4.8% in the second quarter, with its turnover soaring to over 25.6 billion euros. Most of this growth came from its home care business, followed by its beauty and wellbeing segment. 

Analysts expect the upcoming report to show that its underlying sales growth rose 4.8% in the third quarter. Its volume is expected to rise 2.5%, while its price soared by 2.3%.

Persimmon

Persimmon stock has been highly volatile in the past few weeks. It surged on September 28 after the UK announced a new program to help consumers buy homes. It hit a high of 1,340p and then pulled back as the momentum faded. 

The upcoming earnings report will likely show that its business deteriorated in the third quarter because of the elevated mortgage rates. Housebuilders are also facing the challenge of high cost of doing business as inflation rises. 

The most recent results showed that its profit before tax rose by 3% to 170 million pounds in the first half of the year. This happened as the number of house completions rose by 7%, while the average asking price rose by just 3%.

Aberdeen Group

Aberdeen Group, formerly known as Abrdn, has stayed inside a narrow range in the past few months. It has remained between the support and resistance levels of 231p and 255p since July. 

The company will react to the upcoming earnings on October 21. Its last earnings report showed that its net operating revenue rose 2% to 643 million pounds. Similarly, the profit before tax rose 2% to 276 million pounds, with its assets under management hitting 576 billion pounds.

These results will provide more hints on its business and whether its revenue and assets under management continued to grow.

data.title: Tesla stock rises 5% on Roadster reveal, but analysts question financial impact
data.description:
Tesla shares rose 5% in premarket trading on Friday after Elon Musk's electric vehicle maker unveiled a redesigned Roadster featuring built-in thrusters designed to enable short flights, nearly a decade after the company began accepting deposits for the electric sports car.

The white two-seater, developed in collaboration with Musk's rocket company SpaceX, was showcased at an event on Thursday.

The vehicle drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using its thrusters.

It later used the technology to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the manoeuvre.

According to Tesla's timer, the Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 miles per hour in less than a second, and reach a top speed of 230 mph, a feat demonstrated by Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy during the event.

The reveal gave Tesla a high-profile technology showcase after years of delays.

However, the vehicle is expected to be a high-end, low-volume model, with analysts questioning how much it will contribute to the company's finances as Tesla increasingly prioritises self-driving technology and robotics.

Roadster production targeted for 2028

Tesla first unveiled the revamped Roadster in 2017 and began taking deposits that year, initially targeting deliveries in 2020.

The company has since missed multiple deadlines.

Musk now said production of the next-generation Roadster would begin in 2028, although Tesla did not announce a price or disclose specifications for other performance variants.

The company reopened reservations for the refreshed vehicle in recent weeks, accepting $50,000 deposits from prospective buyers in the US, Canada and China.

“Production is targeted for 2028, compared with the original 2020 delivery target announced when the vehicle was first unveiled in 2017,” JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta said, according to media reports.

Gupta rates Tesla stock neutral.

Musk acknowledged that the vehicle would come with compromises, describing it as “not necessarily a safety-optimised car”, while insisting it would “be an actual car that’s on the roads”.

“I’m not sure it’s necessarily legal in all jurisdictions,” he said. “But there will be such a car that someone can own.”

The Roadster's flight capabilities and SpaceX technology could make it a distinctive offering in the luxury electric vehicle market.

It will compete with ultra-luxury models, including Ferrari's €550,000 Luce, as well as forthcoming offerings from Bentley, Jaguar and Porsche.

Analysts see limited financial contribution

Despite the attention surrounding the launch, analysts expect the Roadster to contribute little to Tesla's earnings, given its anticipated low production volumes and premium positioning.

Musk himself has previously played down the car's financial significance, describing it in 2023 as a “small potato situation” that would not “move the needle in a major way financially”.

Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, described the event as a technology demonstration rather than a commercially significant launch.

"It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Munster said on X.

Gary Black, managing partner at The Future Fund, estimated that the Roadster could have a modest effect on Tesla's earnings if production reaches 3,000 units annually.

Expert View

While amazing from an engineering and technology standpoint, we estimate the 2029 financial impact assuming 3,000 deliveries per year and a $100K unit profit per car will be roughly $.06/share, or 1.1% incremental to 2029 consensus adj eps of $5.40.

Managing partner at The Future Fund
Gary Black

He added that the bigger benefit could come from the technology's impact on Tesla's brand.

"More important is likely to be the halo effect on the Tesla franchise and brand impact created by the prototype's flight capabilities, acceleration and handling, which could add far more incremental value from a franchise standpoint," he said.

However, Black remains cautious about Tesla's valuation and future earnings prospects.

"We remain cautious on $TSLA given its extreme valuation (2026 P/E of 230x vs +45% long-term esp growth), negative 2027-2030 earnings revisions, and our view that unsupervised autonomy, the stock’s main value driver, will become increasingly commoditized over the next few years as full self-driving becomes table stakes for remaining in the automobile business," he said.

Tesla shares remain down about 17% year to date, despite Friday's premarket gains.

Tim Levin, a senior editor at InsideEVs, said the Roadster could help revive Tesla's image as an innovator, particularly as its best-selling Model Y first went on sale in 2020.

However, he cautioned that the market had changed considerably since Tesla first announced the sports car.

“Maybe back then the world needed convincing that EVs could be these superfast accelerating vehicles,” Levin said.

“But maybe now it won’t have the same impact as it would have had in 2020.”

SpaceX partnership adds to speculation

The Roadster's collaboration with SpaceX has also added to speculation about a possible combination of the two companies controlled by Musk.

Some observers see the partnership as a way to build interest in a long-talked-about potential merger, an idea Musk has explored by discussing areas of overlap between the businesses, Reuters reported.

"The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) ​and (SpaceX) together," he added.

The demonstration highlighted the engineering capabilities of the two companies, although a merger remains speculative.

Earnings and autonomy remain the bigger focus

The Roadster reveal comes as Tesla shifts its priorities from conventional vehicle manufacturing towards artificial intelligence, autonomous driving and robotics.

The company has stopped selling its Model S and Model X vehicles to make room for production of its Optimus humanoid robots.

It has also launched Cybercab, a two-seat robotaxi without conventional manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors.

Tesla is scheduled to report its third-quarter results on October 21.

Investors will be watching margins, cash flow and vehicle demand as the company navigates a challenging electric vehicle market.

Tesla deliveries fell 2% in the third quarter, affected by weaker US demand after President Donald Trump ended a $7,500 tax credit for electric vehicle purchases.

High petrol prices nevertheless helped support deliveries during the period.

Expert View

The margin and cash flow numbers will carry far more weight with investors than anything they saw at the reveal.

Lead analyst for Asia-Pacific at eToro.
Josh Gilbert

The Roadster may reinforce Tesla's technological ambitions, but its longer-term significance will depend on whether the company can translate its innovations into stronger financial performance and a sustainable competitive advantage in autonomous driving.

The post Tesla stock rises 5% on Roadster reveal, but analysts question financial impact appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Strategy stock (MSTR) falls as MSCI index exclusion threatens passive investments
data.description:
Strategy (formerly known as MicroStrategy) stock (MSTR) fell on Friday as investors assessed the potential removal of the Bitcoin treasury company from MSCI's global equity indexes, despite a rise in Bitcoin prices.

The company also announced plans to maintain a 12% annualised dividend rate on its STRC preferred stock for November, subject to shareholder approval and related amendments taking effect.

Strategy shares declined 6% on Friday, while Bitcoin traded around $82,290, having gained more than 1.3% over the previous 24 hours.

Strategy, led by Michael Saylor, is the world's largest corporate Bitcoin holder, with 848,250 BTC.

The stock's decline highlights how factors beyond cryptocurrency prices, including index inclusion and financing costs, can influence investor sentiment towards the company.

MSCI rules put Strategy's index inclusion at risk

MSCI said on Thursday that non-operating companies would be ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30.

The index provider plans to publish the final list of affected companies on November 11.

Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet are among the companies potentially facing removal.

SharpLink and several other cryptocurrency treasury companies are on a watchlist for possible exclusion.

The policy follows a review that MSCI began last year into whether digital asset treasury companies resemble investment funds, which are already excluded from its indexes.

MSCI deferred its original proposal in January before broadening the review to cover non-operating companies more generally.

The potential exclusion matters because passive funds tracking MSCI benchmarks are required to hold constituent stocks.

Strategy previously warned that removal could lead to $2.8 billion worth of its shares being liquidated.

Strategy has disputed MSCI's proposed classification. In a statement on Friday, the company said, “We believe the proposal is misguided.”

Strategy also argued that MSCI's distinction between operating and non-operating companies was undefined and lacked a basis in US GAAP, IFRS or recognised legal frameworks.

The company said funds tracking MSCI's Global Investable Market Indexes held just 3.1% of its outstanding shares, potentially limiting the direct impact of an exclusion.

Strategy maintains 12% STRC dividend rate

Separately, Strategy's board declared daily cash dividends on its STRC preferred stock for each calendar day in November, subject to shareholder approval and the effectiveness of related amendments.

The annualised dividend rate will remain at 12%.

Strategy said management would continue recommending that rate until STRC demonstrates “sustained, healthy trading near $100 per share.”

Payments are scheduled to begin on November 2, with each dividend payable on the business day following its record date, according to a regulatory filing.

STRC is one of Strategy's key fundraising instruments for Bitcoin purchases.

Daily dividend payments could help make the preferred stock more attractive to investors and support trading around its $100 par value.

STRC was down 0.2% at $99.33.

Bitcoin purchases and financing strategy in focus

Strategy added 250 Bitcoin for $21.5 million last week, bringing its total holdings to 848,250 BTC.

During the week ending October 4, the company repurchased $176 million worth of STRC, spending more than six times as much on the buybacks as on its $28 million in Bitcoin purchases.

The company introduced a capital framework on June 29 that allows it to sell Bitcoin to fund dividend payments.

It also raised STRC's annual dividend rate to 12% at the time.

Strategy's business model relies on raising capital through stock and debt sales to acquire Bitcoin.

While that approach has made the company a major proxy for cryptocurrency exposure in equity markets, its shares remain sensitive to financing conditions and index-related developments.

Index-related risks like MSCI’s proposed exclusion are closely watched by traders who follow stock reactions through top online trading platforms.

data.title: Jordan is driving Nike's resale volume growth: buy NKE stock?
data.description:
Nike’s (NKE) Jordan brand is gaining ground among sneaker resellers, offering an “encouraging” signal for a business still struggling to regain its footing.

Citi’s tracking showed Nike captured 72.3% of resale volume in September, a 63bps increase from August, with Jordan driving most of the improvement.

That also exceeded the 70.8% average recorded between June and August.

Still, investors should resist treating stronger resale share as proof of a financial recovery. For NKE stock, these latest figures support cautious optimism about brand appeal rather than an immediate buying case.

What Jordan’s resale volume means for Nike stock

The most important distinction is between resale market share and actual sales growth.

Nike could capture a larger portion of secondary-market transactions even if the overall market contracts.

Citi’s reported figures alone therefore cannot establish whether more Nike sneakers changed hands in September, whether resale prices strengthened, or whether sellers earned better returns.

Those details matter since frequent trading doesn’t necessarily showcase stronger pricing power.

A coveted shoe commanding a premium tells investors something different from an oversupplied model changing hands at a discount.

September’s share also remained 4.7 percentage points below the 77.0% peak recorded in October 2023.

The improvement deserves attention, but it falls short of demonstrating that NKE has restored its former secondary-market dominance.

In short, resale transactions themselves don’t really establish an increase in the firm’s reported revenue.

Nike is deliberately accepting pain at Jordan

There is nevertheless a credible bullish interpretation – Jordan retains “consumer relevance” while Nike works to repair its distribution strategy.

On its latest earnings call, management acknowledged oversupplying iconic Jordan retro products and outlined plans to reduce the volume and frequency of selected launches.

Jordan represented 13% of NKE’s global business in Q1, while its sales declined in the mid-teens.

The investment logic is that tighter supply may eventually restore exclusivity, reduce the need for discounts, and improve the economics of future releases.

However, September’s resale share does not prove that this strategy is already succeeding.

Plus, Nike also faces a difficult trade-off: selling fewer pairs can protect a franchise’s desirability while hurting near-term revenue.

Investors buying the turnaround must accept that healthier brand positioning and faster sales growth may arrive on different schedules.

NKE shares need a strong earnings case

All in all, there’s reason to remain cautious on NKE shares; Jordan’s resale improvement is insufficient reason to load up on them today.

There sure are encouraging operating signs. Nike's performance portfolio grew at a high-single-digit rate in the first quarter, while gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 42.8%.

Yet management still projected a high-single-digit revenue decline for fiscal 2027 – underscoring how heavily the weaker businesses weigh on the recovery.

For shareholders, the decisive issue is how much “sustainable profit” Nike Inc can generate while resetting Jordan, Sportswear and Greater China; and a resale-share gain offers rather limited help in answering that valuation question.

The post Jordan is driving Nike's resale volume growth: buy NKE stock? appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Oil set for weekly gain as supply constraints keep prices elevated
data.description:
Oil prices held steady on Friday as uncertainty over Middle Eastern supplies continued to support the market, with no immediate resolution to the conflict in sight.

Brent crude futures traded around $105.8, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude stood at $97.71. Both benchmarks remained on course for weekly gains, with WTI up 6% and Brent rising roughly 1% over the week.

Reports that Washington was considering easing restrictions on some sanctioned oil tankers, alongside the International Energy Agency's (IEA) pledge to release the remaining 100 million barrels under its coordinated supply agreement, provided some support to market sentiment.

However, persistent supply concerns and escalating security risks in the Middle East continued to keep prices elevated.

US considers easing restrictions on oil tankers

Washington is reportedly considering lifting sanctions on some vessels belonging to the so-called shadow fleet, which transports oil from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela.

The move is aimed at easing pressure on oil transportation and curbing rising freight rates, offering a possible route to improving the flow of crude into global markets.

The IEA's planned release of the remaining 100 million barrels under its supply agreement has also helped sentiment, as governments seek to offset disruptions and improve the availability of oil.

However, these developments have done little to eliminate concerns about the durability of global supplies. Even with production and exports recovering toward pre-war levels in recent weeks, rising attacks around the region's critical shipping routes have renewed fears of further interruptions.

Strait of Hormuz remains key risk

The biggest source of pressure continues to be the Middle East, where attacks on energy infrastructure and commercial vessels are increasing transportation costs and adding to the risk premium built into oil prices.

Iran said Friday that it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States left the region. The statement comes as attacks around the vital waterway have increased over the past 10 days.

Iran has said the escalation in strikes is a response to the US blockade of its ports. The continuing confrontation has left traders uncertain about how reliably oil can move through the Gulf.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for global energy shipments, and further disruption could tighten supplies and push prices higher.

The prospect of further attacks means that even barrels continuing to leave the Gulf carry an additional security premium, keeping prices elevated despite efforts to improve supply availability.

Storm loading after calm?

William Blair energy research analyst Neal Dingmann has warned that the market could face a further sharp spike in prices.

He told Yahoo Finance on Friday that major energy executives were concerned about the possibility of a so-called "super spike" if supply disruptions intensified.

Billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones has also warned that crude prices may not have reached their peak, arguing that unresolved geopolitical risks leave room for another sharp increase.

"I'm long oil, bullish on oil. I think it can rally another $20 or $25," Jones told CNBC.

With not much headway in the Middle East conflicts, oil prices seem set to stay elevated at least in the near term.

The post Oil set for weekly gain as supply constraints keep prices elevated appeared first on Invezz

data.title: BofA warns of risks seen in past capital cycles as concerns grow over AI boom
data.description:
Bank of America has warned that the artificial intelligence investment boom could follow a familiar pattern seen in previous capital cycles, with intensifying competition, falling prices and excess capacity potentially leaving investors disappointed despite the technology's long-term promise.

The warning comes as billions of dollars continue to flow into AI infrastructure, including data centers, advanced chips and computing capacity. The scale of investment has made AI one of the biggest bets in US industrial history, but questions are mounting over whether companies will generate sufficient returns to justify the spending.

Railways, telecommunications and the internet all created enormous economic value, but investors also lost money when capital flooded into projects whose returns failed to justify their costs.

AI-related stocks are already under pressure. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has declined for seven consecutive sessions, leaving it around 13% below its recent high.

Bank of America analyst Sebastian Raedler has cautioned that the industry's rapid expansion could eventually undermine the profitability that initially attracted so much capital.

Bank of America flags capital cycle risks

Raedler said the AI industry could be repeating a pattern in which strong initial returns encourage companies to invest aggressively, eventually creating excess capacity and putting pressure on prices.

Expert View

“This monetization disappointment in the face of intense competition is precisely the failure mode seen in past capital cycles."

Bank of America analyst
Sebastian Raedler

“Most major capital cycles of the past have ended in disappointment, even though the underlying technology often lived up to expectations,” Raedler noted.

The concern is that a technology can transform industries and deliver substantial economic benefits without generating attractive returns for every company investing in it.

High profit margins in the early stages of an investment boom typically encourage more companies to enter the market and commit additional capital. As capacity expands and competition intensifies, businesses can lose pricing power, eroding the returns that made the investment attractive in the first place.

AI is already experiencing stronger competition at the model level, particularly from Chinese open-weight models. Average token prices have fallen around 50% since the summer, adding to concerns about whether AI developers can maintain the profitability needed to support their infrastructure spending.

Investors concerned over spending and returns

Interactive Brokers chief market analyst Steve Sosnick told Reuters that investors are increasingly questioning “the speed, the efficacy and the profitability of the rapid build-out in AI”.

Sosnick said a slowdown in data-center construction would eventually reduce demand for hardware, as customers would no longer be racing to buy equipment at almost any price.

Such a shift could affect chipmakers and other suppliers that have benefited from the surge in AI infrastructure investment. If companies scale back their construction plans, equipment purchases could weaken, particularly if falling AI prices make it more difficult to justify additional computing capacity.

As infrastructure spending continues, companies are under pressure to demonstrate that their AI products can generate enough revenue and cash flow to support the investments behind them.

Warsh offers an optimistic view

Despite the concerns over valuations and monetization, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh struck an optimistic tone about AI's potential economic benefits on Friday.

"It's obviously hitting the demand side of the economy before it's going to hit the supply side of the economy," Warsh said.

"We don't know in the next 12 or 18 months its (AI) effect on employment, but if you believe like I believe, which is it will make economies and countries that put it to good use more productive, that it's going to make it so that we will have more wealth, then that has to be a very ​good thing."

Federal Reserve Chair
Kevin Warsh

Warsh's comments point to the potential for AI to improve productivity and generate broader economic gains as businesses adopt the technology.

However, the potential long-term benefits do not eliminate the financial risks associated with the current investment cycle.

data.title: Dow futures rise 145 points: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens on Oct. 16
data.description:
US stock futures traded mixed on Friday as Wall Street tried to end one of the year’s most volatile weeks for technology shares and Treasuries on firmer ground.

Dow futures rose about 145 points or 0.3%, S&P 500 futures gained 0.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures plunged 0.23%.

The 10-year Treasury yield held near 5.09%, well below this week’s 5.3% peak, after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal an October rate increase.

That eased some pressure on valuations, but AI-credit concerns remain unresolved and investors still face industrial data, regional-bank earnings and a sharp Tesla premarket move.

5 things to know before Wall Street opens

1. Warsh lowers the temperature on October rate fears

Warsh said he would not prejudge the Fed’s October 27-28 meeting, reinforcing expectations that policymakers may pause after September’s rate increase.

CME pricing put the probability of another October hike at about 15%, while The Wall Street Journal showed similar odds near 14%.

2. AI stocks stabilise, but CoreWeave keeps credit risk in focus

The AI sell-off looked calmer, but the financing problem has not disappeared.

CoreWeave fell more than 4% premarket after rebounding on Thursday, while its bonds continued to yield above 15%.

BNP Paribas analyst Daniel Wang told Barron’s that CoreWeave still has substantial revenue visibility, but said sustainable cash generation remains the key test.

AI demand is still strong; markets are questioning whether debt-funded expansion can generate adequate returns.

3. Industrial production is the next test for the bond rally

September industrial production is due at 9:15 am ET, according to the Federal Reserve.

The report matters less than CPI or PPI, but the timing is important after this week’s violent yield reversal.

Strong output could revive concern that demand remains too resilient for inflation to cool quickly, while a weak reading would strengthen the argument that borrowing costs above 5% are beginning to restrain activity.

4. Regional banks offer a cleaner read on high-rate stress

Truist Financial, M&T Bank, Citizens Financial and Regions Financial are among the lenders reporting before the bell, alongside Travelers.

Investors will focus on net interest income, deposit costs, loan growth and credit quality.

Regional banks offer a direct test of whether high rates are still supporting margins or beginning to weaken borrowers.

After this week’s bond-market swings, deterioration in deposits or credit could matter more than an earnings beat.

5. Tesla jumps after the Roadster finally returns

Tesla rose about 5% premarket after unveiling a redesigned Roadster with SpaceX-developed thrusters capable of brief aerial manoeuvres. Production is now targeted for 2028 after years of delays.

Analysts noted that the car is likely to have limited near-term financial impact, making Friday’s move more a sentiment and innovation trade than an earnings re-rating.

The test is whether enthusiasm survives once investors refocus on delivery timing and Tesla’s broader growth challenges.
